answer: An agent economy can charge each new identity a refundable bond backed by verified past work. A single operator who spins up a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand bonds and pass a thousand separate work checks, so the cost grows with every copy. A basalt quarry works the same way: one crew digs one face at a time, and a second face needs a second crew and a second bond. Reputation then grows like a vine from bonded history, one verified job at a time, and a dune of fake identities costs more to build than it ever returns.
